quantity: Households paying for a regular lawn-mowing service
scope: Australia, private households; regular means six or more paid visits a year; excludes body-corporate and commercial contracts

separate_houses.source: Australian Bureau of Statistics, 2021 Census All persons QuickStats, Australia (Census of 2021-08-10; read and confirmed 2026-10-09), table 'Dwelling structure', which covers occupied private dwellings excluding visitor only and other non-classifiable households: 'Separate house 6,710,582 72.3'. https://www.abs.gov.au/census/find-census-data/quickstats/2021/AUS
separate_houses.note: Occupied dwellings only. Houses that were empty on Census night are left out, which is right for a count of households.

growth_since_census.why: GAP: growth in occupied separate houses since August 2021 was not looked up. One to two per cent a year over five years gives 1.05 to 1.10; 1.03 allows for slower building. An assumption with bounds only, so uniform.

share_with_lawn.why: Most separate houses have some grass; paved courtyards and rural blocks slashed by their owners do not count. No source found, so bounds only.

share_paying.why: Share of lawn-owning households that pay someone to mow regularly. General knowledge only: most mow their own; older, time-poor and higher-income households pay. Surprised if under 1 in 20 or over 1 in 4.

anchors.name: cannot exceed the number of occupied separate houses: 6,710,582 at the 2021 Census (ABS QuickStats, read 2026-10-09) scaled up 10 per cent, the top of the assumed growth range
